audit.whatIsWrong: Darkness Rise is never mentioned in either layer, despite being the reason short trades beat long ones here.
audit.why: Mordekaiser's passive only switches on after he lands three attacks or spells on a champion. Breaking off at two denies the aura entirely. For a champion whose whole trade pattern is walk-up, stack, disengage, that is the single most actionable fact in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Break off at two hits — Darkness Rise only ignites on the third.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers treat Devour as one thing. It has two entirely different cost profiles depending on target.
audit.why: Devour deals damage to an enemy champion and shields an ally. The three-stack An Acquired Taste requirement applies to devouring an enemy; peeling an ally carries no such prerequisite. A player who believes he needs stacks to peel will hold the ability when it was free to use.
audit.corrected: Devour needs three stacks on an enemy but none on an ally — the peel is always available, the eat is not.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] and wants.you[0] teach 'stun him, and Devour' / 'then stun and Devour' as a single sequence.
audit.why: Tongue Lash on a three-stack target stuns and consumes the stacks; devouring an enemy champion requires three stacks. One set of stacks pays for one of the two.
audit.corrected: Three stacks buys the Q-stun or the Devour, not both.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero sequencing cues for this matchup and no real cooldown appears anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Realm of Death is the matchup's whole threat and it is 140s at rank 1 — surviving one is worth more than two minutes of free side lane, but nothing tells the player that. Death's Grasp at 16s rank 1 is the other punishable cooldown.
audit.corrected: Realm of Death 140/120/100s. Death's Grasp 16/14/12/10/8s at 700 range. Obliterate 8/7/6/5/4s at 675, biggest on an isolated target. Indestructible 12/11/10/9/8s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds is never mentioned in the content layer, though wants.foe[2] describes exactly the problem it solves.
audit.why: Indestructible stores damage Mordekaiser deals and takes, then converts it to healing, on an 8s cooldown at rank 5. Against a Tahm Kench win condition built on attrition, un-answered healing means the kill window never opens. The missing-interactions file flags this matchup for anti-heal.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal timing decides extended trades against Indestructible.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid and content.late both route Tahm Kench's level 6 through 'Abyssal Voyage' — global utility, re-entering lane after a recall, contesting objectives across the map.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-rework ultimate and is absent from the current kit. Level 6 gives Devour. The reposition is Abyssal Dive (W), available from level 2 on a 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown. The advice as written promises a map tool the champion does not have.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Devour, not an escape; Abyssal Dive has been the reposition since level 2.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json W Abyssal Dive, R Devour

audit.why: 50.51% over 1275 games and the chart reads Mordekaiser 4 / Skill 3 / Tahm Kench 0. Mordekaiser-sided through the ultimate window with an even finish matches both the prose (whys[6], spikes[3] both call full build 'genuinely even') and the headline number. The packet did not flag a chart contradiction here. Left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mordekaiser's Q Obliterate carries a derived 'grounding' flag in the kit file. It should not be used.
audit.why: The flag is a parsing artefact from the phrase 'smashes the ground' in Riot's description text. Nothing in the ability's stated effect grounds anyone. I did not build any advice on it.
audit.corrected: No edit made — flagged so the derivation can be fixed upstream.

edits.before: Mordekaiser's E pull comes online — if he lands it and follows with Q's isolated bonus slam, you take a massive chunk before your 3-stack stun is even relevant.
edits.after: Death's Grasp comes online — if he pulls and follows with Obliterate's isolated bonus, you lose a chunk before your 3-stack stun matters. It is 16s at rank 1.

edits.before: Your 3-stack stun into Devour is your best punish window — land Tongue Lash, stack An Acquired Taste on his approach, stun him, and Devour before his W shield absorbs the burst.
edits.after: Three stacks is your punish window, but it buys the Q-stun or the Devour, not both — and either way spend it while Indestructible is on cooldown, never into a live shield.

edits.before: Land 3 An Acquired Taste stacks before he closes range with E, then stun and Devour to remove him from the trade window
edits.after: Land 3 An Acquired Taste stacks before Death's Grasp closes the gap, then spend them on the stun or on Devour — they pay once

edits.before: Activate Thick Skin's shield during his Q isolated slam to absorb the burst and immediately reset grey health out of combat
edits.after: Activate Thick Skin's shield during Obliterate's isolated slam to absorb the burst, then break combat fully so grey health converts

edits.before: Land his E pull to interrupt your stack-fishing and immediately follow with Q's isolated bonus damage before you can react
edits.after: Land Death's Grasp to interrupt your stack-fishing and follow with Obliterate's isolated bonus before you can answer it

edits.before: Stack his W shield and heal off your Tongue Lash poke so your sustained attrition never actually opens a kill window
edits.after: Feed Indestructible on damage dealt and taken, then heal it off — without Grievous Wounds your attrition never opens a kill

edits.before: Mordekaiser has no E at level 1, so neither of you has a decisive opener — fish Tongue Lash stacks safely and let Thick Skin bank grey health from his autos.
edits.after: Without Death's Grasp at level 1 neither of you has an opener — fish Tongue Lash stacks and break off at two hits, since Darkness Rise only ignites on his third.

edits.before: He can now E pull you into Q isolated slam before your 3-stack stun answers it — respect his engage range and don't auto-push into his face.
edits.after: Death's Grasp pulls you into an isolated Obliterate before your 3-stack stun answers — 700 range, 16s at rank 1, so a missed pull is a free walk-up.

edits.before: His first AP item deepens the R-kill threat and he outscales your first-item tankiness in the 1v1 stat-steal scenario; avoid solo-duel situations without Flash.
edits.after: His first AP item deepens the R-kill threat, but Realm of Death is 140s at rank 1 — once he has spent it, the next two minutes of side lane belong to you.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are Mordekaiser's window even before his ultimate: his Q damage on isolated targets is meaningful, his W sustain lets him sit in extended trades, and you have no ultimate escape if he chains E into Q repeatedly. Play for CS and opportunistic stack-fishing rather than forcing all-ins — activate Thick Skin to shield when he steps in with E, don't let him dictate the trade length with his sustained healing. Level 6 is the most important spike to respect: Realm of Death disables your Devour entirely and steals your tankiness, so the moment he hits 6 you must treat Flash as your anti-R tool and hug the outer half of the lane. Your own level 6 Abyssal Voyage adds global utility and lets you re-enter the lane fresh after a recall, but it does not flip the 1v1.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are Mordekaiser's window even before his ultimate: Obliterate's isolated damage is meaningful, Indestructible lets him sit in extended trades, and you cannot disengage if he chains Death's Grasp into Obliterate repeatedly. Play for CS and opportunistic stack-fishing rather than forcing all-ins — shield with Thick Skin when he steps in with the pull, and break off at two hits so Darkness Rise never ignites. Level 6 is the most important spike to respect: Realm of Death disables your Devour entirely and steals your tankiness, so the moment he hits 6 you must treat Flash as your anti-R tool and hug the outer half of the lane. Your own level 6 is Devour, not an escape — Abyssal Dive has been your reposition since level 2, on a 21s cooldown.

edits.before: Past first item the lane reaches a genuine equilibrium: your Heartsteel and Sunfire Aegis stacking means your grey-health healing and Thick Skin shield absorb what his Q throws at you, and he can no longer cleanly Realm-of-Death kill you if you've been farming HP all game — your base stats simply become too high for his stat-steal to swing the duel. Your job shifts to being the immovable frontline in teamfights: peel your carries with Devour, land stun-into-Devour on his fed backline, and use Abyssal Voyage to contest objectives across the map. He is equally unkillable but has no mobility and no peel — a 50/50 that resolves in your team's favor if you out-rotate him.
edits.after: Past first item the lane reaches a genuine equilibrium: your Heartsteel and Sunfire Aegis stacking means your grey-health healing and Thick Skin shield absorb what Obliterate throws at you, and he can no longer cleanly Realm-of-Death kill you if you've been farming HP all game — your base stats simply become too high for his stat-steal to swing the duel. Your job shifts to being the immovable frontline: Devour shields an ally for free, while eating his carry costs you three stacks, so know which one you are holding it for. He is equally unkillable but has no mobility and no peel — a 50/50 that resolves in your team's favor if you out-rotate him.

edits.before: Build MR — Q-stun him, W-dodge his realm combo. Tahm Kench wins the Realm of Death cooldown windows.
edits.after: Build MR — three stacks buys a Q-stun or a Devour. Tahm Kench wins the 140-second Realm of Death window.

edits.before: Build MR and Q-stun him. Track Realm of Death before every commit and keep the wave on your side.
edits.after: Build MR and Q-stun him. Track Realm of Death's 140s and Death's Grasp's 16s before you commit.

edits.before: Q-stun at 3 stacks is your kill switch. Only take the trade when Mordekaiser's Realm of Death is down.
edits.after: Q-stun at 3 stacks is your kill switch. Break off at two hits so Darkness Rise never turns on.

edits.before: Devour deletes him from the fight — or you from his. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Mordekaiser's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Devour needs three stacks on an enemy but none on an ally. Realm of Death is 140s at rank 1 — surviving it buys two minutes.

edits.before: - Mordekaiser Realm of Death: matchup-defining — His 1v1 realm. W-dive resets in it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Realm of Death: 140s at rank 1, 100s at rank 3 — his whole threat, and your two free minutes after it. - Death's Grasp: 16s at rank 1, 700 range — the pull that starts everything. - Obliterate: 8s, worst when you are alone.

edits.before: Get isolated low in his R. Stand in his E. Fight low in the realm. Don't spend your ultimate on chip — it is the kill window.
edits.after: Get caught low in his R. Stand in Death's Grasp. Trade past two hits and let Darkness Rise ignite. Skip anti-heal into Indestructible.

edits.before: - Tahm Kench vs Mordekaiser - Track: Mordekaiser Realm of Death. - Keep the wave on your side. - Engage only on Realm of Death's cooldown. - Don't chase past the wave. - Ultimate = kill windows only.
edits.after: - Tahm Kench vs Mordekaiser - Track: Realm of Death 140s, Death's Grasp 16s. - Break off at two hits — Darkness Rise needs three. - Three stacks = Q-stun OR Devour. - Bring anti-heal.
